$description: MetaTV 'Graphite' palette — the NEUTRAL dark theme. Identical role structure to Midnight; it differs only in its scale choices, which is the entire point of the restructure: a theme is a handful of hue picks, not 140 hand-authored values. Its decorative hues are a PAIRWISE SWAP of Midnight's, declared in $scales — which doubles as a hue substitution table, so re-hueing a whole theme is eight lines rather than 40 edited values.

container.$description: controls at rest, chips with a fill

on-surface.$description: TWO text roles, not five. The old palette had 15 neutrals named dim/muted/faint/disabled/low — named by APPEARANCE, which gives no rule for which to use, so every new widget picked a new one. Radix publishes exactly two text steps (11 low-contrast, 12 high-contrast) and Material 3 names exactly two roles, because that is how many text roles actually exist. The rest below are non-text states and are exempt from the 4.5:1 floor by definition, not by exception.

strong.$description: titles — the loudest text in a row

disabled.$description: NOT text — a disabled control (WCAG exempts these)

placeholder.$description: NOT text — empty-field hint / absent-image glyph

meta.$description: Neutral row metadata. Deliberately NOT under facet.*: these carry no hue encoding, and putting them there made two of them share a colour, which for a hue-encoded facet would be a false statement about the data.

default.$description: Step 8, not 9: indigo.9 against this palette's light ink measures 4.49:1 — under the floor by 0.01, which the selection-readability guard catches. A near miss is still a miss.

on.$description: foreground ON a solid primary fill. NEAR-BLACK, not white: blue.9 is a light blue, so white on it measures 2.81:1 — the conventional dark-theme look and genuinely hard to read. This repeats a lesson already learned once at COLOR_ON_ACCENT, and the conformance test is what caught me repeating it.

scrim.$description: Alpha overlays. These are Radix ALPHA steps, not hand-mixed rgba() — the old OVERLAY_* family was 39 tokens over 16 base colours with hand-picked alphas.

facet.$description: Data-category hues. One hue per facet, and NO TWO FACETS SHARE A HUE — the mockup review caught language and platform reading as the same thing. Step 11 keeps every one of them >=4.5:1 as text on surface.base.

language-fill.$description: language keeps a FILL — owner's call: it is the highest-value facet after the title

quality.$description: One DISTINCT hue per tier, which is what the hand-tuned palette already did (purple UHD / blue FHD / teal HD / yellow LIVE). A first draft here ramped them within one hue instead — and the palette conformance suite immediately failed it, because tiers a user must tell apart at a glance cannot differ only in lightness. Step 11 keeps every one of them >=4.5:1 as outline text. Quality is a claim about THIS copy, so it renders by the title, not in the right rail.
